# UIAO OrgPath {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
This series was formerly titled **"OrgPath Narrative."** The slug, URLs, and
file paths are unchanged; only the display name now carries the `UIAO` program
prefix. Older cross-references to the "OrgPath Narrative" point here.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}

::: {.callout-note appearance="default"}
## Companion series — the implementation guides
This series is the *what* and *why*. Its companion, the **[OrgPath Implementation Guides — Intune & Azure Arc](../operational-guides/orgpath-implementation/index.qmd)**, is the *how*: a command-by-command path from an empty tenant to OrgPath facets landing on Intune-managed devices and Azure Arc-enrolled servers, governed by a drift loop.
:::

A seventeen-document reading sequence written in continuous narrative voice —
no bullets, no itemization, no machine-style decomposition. The series
examines the structural gap at the center of the Microsoft cloud identity
stack and the OrgTree / OrgPath governance substrate that closes it.

The early documents do not lead with UIAO. They begin with an architect's
honest accounting of what Microsoft's native identity and governance
products actually provide, then articulate what a governance substrate
must contain to be useful, and finally introduce OrgTree and OrgPath as
the proposed answer. The middle of the sequence walks the OrgPath
attribute through every Microsoft surface that consumes it — Intune,
Defender, Purview, Application Identity, Azure Policy, Cross-Tenant B2B,
Sentinel / PIM / RBAC, DNS / Cloud PKI, Power BI — and the supplement at
the end addresses third-party DDI integration with Infoblox and BlueCat.
A 07a supplement immediately after the Purview chapter develops the
identity-substrate role UIAO plays beneath Microsoft Fabric, OneLake,
and Purview as the Azure SSOT stack. The fifteenth document is the
synthesis: the UIAO Governance OS narrative that ties the series
together. A sixteenth document closes the arc as a practical coda —
grounding the whole substrate on the real Windows Server 2025 host,
running Gitea behind IIS inside the boundary, where canon physically
lives — and points to the canonical build runbook for the procedure
itself. A seventeenth book extends the substrate to the network edge —
the RADIUS, 802.1X, and NAC admission plane Microsoft left to the
network — binding OrgPath into the moment a device first requests a
network address, as the third policy-targeting transport alongside
Intune and Azure Policy.

The documents are published here unchanged from their authored form.
Each carries Quarto front matter for site rendering and DOCX export, but
the prose body is the original manuscript without revision. Where a
document references a UIAO architectural decision or canon artifact,
readers should consult the linked canon for the normative version; this
series is the explanatory companion.

## Companion canon

For the normative substrate specifications and architectural decisions
this narrative paraphrases:

- [Modernization → OrgTree](/customer-documents/reference-architecture/orgtree.html) — the
  canonical OrgTree / OrgPath specification (`UIAO_007`).
- [Architecture Decision Records](/docs/adr/index.html) — the binding
  record of UIAO architectural decisions. The OrgPath substrate is
  governed primarily by `ADR-035` (codebook binding), `ADR-036` (dynamic
  group provisioning), `ADR-037` (administrative unit provisioning),
  `ADR-038` (device-plane OrgPath), `ADR-039` (policy targeting),
  `ADR-040` (drift engine), `ADR-041` (UIAO Git infrastructure), and
  `ADR-048` (OrgPath attribute selection).

## A worked consumer — SQL Server

The substrate exists to be consumed. The
[SQL Server Identity Transformation](../sql-server-narrative/index.qmd) series is
the first end-to-end worked example: it migrates a SQL Server estate off Active
Directory and onto Entra ID, and at its access-control core it consumes the
OrgPath dynamic-group model this series builds. The seams between the two — and
the order to read them in — are set out in
[OrgPath × SQL Server — The Integration Bridge](../sql-server-narrative/bridge-orgpath-sql.qmd).

## Audience

Federal IT architects, governance engineers, authorizing officials, and
program leadership engaged in Active Directory to Entra ID modernization.
The reading sequence assumes operating familiarity with Active Directory,
Entra ID, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Purview, Azure
Policy, and Conditional Access. Readers without that background will get
more from the
[Executive Governance Series](../executive-governance-series/index.qmd)
or the
[Whitepapers](../whitepapers/index.qmd) section first.
